name: pca_factor_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Principal Component Analysis on 1-min returns of NIFTY 50 constituents extracts the main factors driving cross-sectional returns: PC1 ≈ market factor (all stocks move together), PC2 ≈ sector rotation factor (e.g., banks vs IT), PC3+ ≈ idiosyncratic signals. By computing rolling PCA on a 60-bar window and identifying stocks whose residual (unexplained by top 3 PCs) is extreme (> 2 sigma), we find stocks with temporary idiosyncratic dislocations that tend to revert as the factor structure reasserts. The inefficiency exists because real-time PCA on 50 stocks at 1-min frequency requires significant computation and linear algebra knowledge. The edge is in identifying factor-adjusted mispricings rather than raw price moves.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents (all 50 used for PCA; trade those with extreme residuals)
stock_filter: All 50 constituents used for PCA computation; trade those with ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr

indicators.name: Returns_Matrix
indicators.params: 50 x 60 matrix of 1-min returns for all NIFTY 50 stocks

indicators.name: Residual
indicators.params: actual_return - factor_return for each stock (current bar)

indicators.name: Variance_Explained
indicators.params: sum of top 3 PC explained variance ratios

conditions: Residual_Zscore < -2.0 (stock significantly underperforming its factor-explained return — idiosyncratic oversold)
Variance_Explained > 0.50 (top 3 PCs explain > 50% of cross-sectional variance — factor structure is strong)
long.confirmation: Residual_Zscore starts improving: Residual_Zscore > Residual_Zscore[2 bars ago]

conditions: Residual_Zscore > 2.0 (stock significantly outperforming its factor-explained return — idiosyncratic overbought)
short.confirmation: Residual_Zscore starts declining: Residual_Zscore < Residual_Zscore[2 bars ago]

exit.target: Residual_Zscore reverts to 0 (stock returns to factor-explained level)
exit.stop_loss: Residual_Zscore reaches -3.5 for longs / +3.5 for shorts (dislocation worsens)
exit.trailing_stop: None — signal-based exit on residual reversion

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; increase to ₹1.25L if Variance_Explained > 0.65 (strong factor structure implies more reliable residual signals)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; high VIX disrupts the factor structure
filters.time_filter: No entries before 10:15 (need 60 bars for PCA) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: All 50 stocks must have traded in last 10 bars for valid PCA
filters.trend_filter: None — PCA residuals are by construction factor-neutral (market trend removed)
filters.spread_filter: Bid-ask spread < 5 bps on target stock
filters.event_filter: Remove any stock with earnings today from PCA computation (outlier returns corrupt factors)
other_filters: At least 45 of 50 stocks must have complete data for valid PCA

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — real-time PCA on 50 stocks at 1-min frequency is computationally demanding and conceptually sophisticated; statistical arbitrage approach is used by hedge funds but not at this frequency in India

weaknesses: PCA on 60 observations of 50 variables is statistically degenerate (more variables than observations) — the eigenvectors are unstable and can flip sign between windows, causing spurious residual spikes
The residual 'reversion' assumption depends on the factor structure being stable — during sector rotation or macro shocks, the factor structure itself changes, and residuals may not revert
PCA recomputation on each bar for 50 stocks (60x50 matrix eigendecomposition) is O(N³) and may exceed latency budget for real-time 1-min trading without optimized numerical libraries
prior_art: Statistical arbitrage (Avellaneda & Lee 2010); PCA for factor extraction in finance (Connor & Korajczyk 1986); Barra risk model uses PCA; intraday stat-arb discussed in Cont & Kukanov (2017)
notes: Consider using incremental PCA (sklearn.decomposition.IncrementalPCA) for efficient online updates rather than full recomputation. Also consider using only the first 2 PCs and grouping residuals by sector for more interpretable signals.
